title: How GPS depends on Einstein
summary: Position from time signals, why the receiver solves for its own clock bias, the special and general relativistic clock shifts (-7 and +45 microseconds per day), the factory frequency offset, the eccentricity and Sagnac corrections, and ionospheric delay.
questions: Why does a receiver need four satellites rather than three, and what extra thing does it get?
Which relativistic effect is larger for GPS satellites, and which direction does the net effect push their clocks?
If every satellite clock ran fast by the same amount, why would position not drift 10 km a day, and why is relativity still essential?
Why can't the factory frequency offset handle the eccentricity correction, and where is it applied instead?
How does a dual-frequency receiver remove most of the ionospheric delay?

title: Kahneman and Tversky: what they found, and what survived
summary: The partnership, heuristics and biases (representativeness, availability, anchoring, regression to the mean), prospect theory and framing, and which findings survived the replication crisis.
questions: In the Linda problem, why is 'bank teller and feminist' a logical error, and which heuristic explains it?
The flight instructor concluded punishment beats praise. What was actually going on, and why does the mistake reinforce itself?
In the Asian disease problem the options are identical but preferences flip. Explain why using prospect theory.
Why did anchoring and framing survive the replication crisis while social priming mostly didn't? What statistical features separate them?
According to Kahneman and Klein, when can expert intuition be trusted, and does a stock picker's environment qualify?
